reason: The cited code sends a fixed browser_hover socket message, then returns a browser-derived ARIA snapshot including the current page URL, title, and snapshot text. Returning browser page state can expose non-public page data from authenticated/local/intranet contexts, so SECRET is supported. The same returned page title/snapshot/URL can be controlled by a visited web page, so UNTRUSTED is supported. The lines do not show arbitrary host code execution. They also do not show agent-supplied data being sent to an attacker-chosen/readable destination; the socket messages are fixed internal browser commands, so SINK is not supported.
